frequency_question: How often does a complex omnibus energy bill pass through all required legislative stages and reach enactment within a single short congressional window (less than 90 days)?
membership_rule: Includes major energy policy acts, comprehensive permitting reform bills, and major budget reconciliation packages containing extensive structural infrastructure provisions; excludes routine appropriations and minor single-agency authorizations.

cases.name: Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 15 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (3.0x)
coverage_note: 5 named major hits; estimated 10 additional major comprehensive energy reform attempts that stalled or failed to pass completely.
known_gaps: Does not account for the specific truncated timeline of a lame-duck session or pre-deadline rush of 78 days, which compresses standard committee and floor timelines.
skeleton: Major energy legislative pushes since 1995: 5 major enactments across 15 significant legislative attempts where comprehensive energy reform was seriously pursued.
multiplier: 5 hits divided by 15 serious attempts equals historical enactment base rate of 33 percent for comprehensive energy packages when introduced.
validity_reason: Legislative procedures and rules governing the filibuster, committee markup, and floor scheduling remain stable across multiple Congresses.
